claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I have one child I'd like to check on - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I've been wanting to claim Child Benefit for him but I'm not entirely sure if I'm eligible or what I need to do.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great that you're looking into this for Alex. Let me gather a bit more detail to assess his eligibility properly.

**To start: Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

(I need to understand your immigration status, as this affects Child Benefit eligibility.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen. I've lived here all my life.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. Now let me ask about Alex's situation:

**Does Alex live with you full-time, or does he live with someone else for part of the time (such as with another parent or guardian)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! That's helpful to know. Now I have a few more questions about Alex's circumstances:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education, or does he have any other status such as being in hospital, in local authority care, or working/training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, there is something I should mention - he was in local authority care for a little while recently, just a couple of months. But he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important detail. That's useful context. Let me clarify:

**When Alex was in local authority care a couple of months ago, how long did he stay in care - was it for a few weeks, or longer than that?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was about 7 weeks in total.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. Now I need to understand the current situation better:

**Since Alex has been back home with you now, has there been any change to his circumstances - for example, is he in full-time education, or is there anything else I should know about his current situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that - he's just a regular 8-year-old at primary school. Everything's pretty normal now that he's back home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that. Before I review the eligibility rules in detail, I just need to check one more thing:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or have you never claimed it before?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I've never claimed it before - that's why I'm asking now. I want to know if I can claim it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess Alex's eligibility. Let me review the official Child Benefit rules to give you an accurate answer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the official Child Benefit eligibility rules, I can now provide you with my assessment:

**You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

1. **You meet the basic eligibility criteria**: You're a British citizen responsible for a child under 16 who lives with you in the UK.

2. **The period in local authority care does not affect your eligibility**: According to the rules, when a child is in care, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if they spend at least 24 hours a week at home. More importantly, since Alex has now returned home and has been back with you, you can claim Child Benefit again. The 8-week limit for continuing payments only applies if the child remains living with someone else after leaving your care.

3. **Alex's current circumstances support eligibility**: He's 8 years old, living with you full-time at home, and in primary school - all of which align with the eligibility requirements.

You should now be able to make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. I'd recommend contacting HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) to submit your claim, and you may want to mention the recent period in care so they have the full picture of his circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to clarify about your eligibility?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Oh that's wonderful news, thank you so much! That's a relief to hear. No, I think you've answered everything I needed to know. I'll get in touch with HMRC to make the claim. Thanks for your help!
